Delhi Police has made extensive security arrangements in the New Delhi area to ensure public safety
in view of the call for protest, Adyantar Mantar by the CJP today.
Police personnel are deployed at multiple checkpoints in New Delhi district, talking
to media deputy commissioner of Delhi Police.
Kumar Abhishek said extensive arrangements have been made to ensure public order is
not disrupted in the area.
He said preventive checks have been implemented in the New Delhi area.
The DCP also informed that some individuals have been detained who are planning to participate
in today's protest.
In New Delhi, in view of the protest that has been declared today, there has been a preventive
check.
There are female staff here and we are checking all the vehicles.
To ensure that there is no disruption to the peace process, we have made all the
necessary arrangements.
Some people have been detained here who are going to participate in today's demonstration.
The Deputy Commissioner of Delhi Traffic Police, Vikas Kumar, said they are facilitating
commuters to take alternate routes as traffic is regulated in the New Delhi area.
He added that traffic police personnel are also guiding people.
Meanwhile, due to security reasons, the entry and exit at 45 metro stations will remain
closed till 6 this evening.
These include Janpat, Patil Chowk, Central Secretariat, Lok Kalyar Marg, Rajiv Chowk,
New Delhi, Seva Tirth and Mandi House.
Interchange facilities will remain available at all the concerned metro stations except
New Delhi metro station.
Namo Bharat train services between Sarai Kale Khan and New Ashok Nagar Namo Bharat
stations in Delhi will also remain closed till 10 p.m. today.
During this period, Namohara train services between Anand Vihar station in Delhi and Modi
Puram station in Uttar Pradesh will continue to operate as per schedule.
Indian Railways has cancelled several trains arriving at New Delhi, Dhillak bridge and
Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4 am and 2 pm today.
According to the railways, all mail and express trains departing from their originating
stations after 2 pm yesterday and scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin
stations. Between 4 a.m. and 2 p.m. today have been cancelled at source. It said the
decision has been taken in view of the anticipated heavy road traffic congestion in areas surrounding
the railway stations.
Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chauhan today alleged that the opposition is weakening
constitutional institutions and raking people's faith in democracy. The union minister claimed
that all this is being done with the support of foreign powers. Addressing a press conference
in Bhopal, he criticized the India bloc and took a dig at the Kokrojanta party without
naming it.
Mr. Chauhan said that on one side the people are standing with Prime Minister Narendra Modi
to build a Vicky Siddharat, while on the other side, the opposition is disappointed
and frustrated.
The opposition cannot win in the electoral arena or on the rest of the people.
That is why it is trying to create chaos on the streets, dismantling constitutional
institutions conspiring to undermine faith in democracy and tearing the
constitution to shreds and the position is not doing all this on its own it is
doing so with the support of foreign powers.
BJP National President Nitin Abhin today alleged that opposition parties are
making efforts to create instability in the country and acting at the
behest of foreign forces. Talking to reporters in New Delhi Mr. Naveen accused
opposition parties of attempting to create a highly dangerous and
serious situation in the country.
Netanyahu also accused the opposition of insulting the public mandate by spreading falsehoods
in the name of the Constitution.
He said repeated electoral defeats had led to desperation among opposition parties.
The BGP President said the government will deal firmly with attempts to create tension
in the country.
Over the past 12 years, under the leadership of the Prime Minister, we have steered the
country, out of an atmosphere of fear and endeavour to eradicate terrorism and naxalism from their
very root.
Yet there are still individuals with an urban naxal mindset who are intent on destabilising
the nation.
The youth of India are deeply connected to the Indian culture and democracy and are
committed to the Indian constitution.
The way you are attempting to challenge the country's constitutional framework and
its democracy and the insulting language you employ against individuals holding the
nation's highest offices will never be accepted by India's 140 crore citizens
and you will certainly face the consequences.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today said India is closely monitoring developments in its
neighbourhood and beyond, along with their strategic implications amid major changes in
modern warfare and the global security order.
Addressing exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 at Jodhpur Air Force Station, the Defence Minister
said the established world order was changing rapidly, while the shape of the emerging
global order remained uncertain.
Added to the uncertainties and unpredictability coming from mind-boggling, the speed of technological
changes in the defence sector is the geopolitical flux.
We are facing a situation where the older, stabilised world order is fast disappearing
while the shape of future order is yet to emerge.
In light of this volatile security environment, a perpetual state of high alertness is
demanded from every responsible nation.
The exercise, begun on September 26, will continue till October 12, besides the Indian
Air Force, Air Forces of seven countries, Australia, the United States, France, Germany, and United
Arab Emirates, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh are participating in the exercise.
The exercise features several advanced fighter jets, including the F-35, Lightning II, Rafale
and F-16, along with transport and aerial refueling aircrafts.
Held under the theme of power in partnership, the exercise aims to enhance interoperability,
strengthen military cooperation and facilitate the exchange of operational expertise among
participating Air Force's Jitendra Dividi, Akashwani News, Jaiipur.
The government has debunked an article claiming that the Indian Air Force suffered losses
during the Balakot Air Strike.
The fact-check unit of the Press Information Bureau, PIB, informed that the article misrepresents
the nature and execution of the operation, presenting a misleading narrative that distorts
the facts.
The unit added that the Balakot Air Strike was a deliberate, targeted operation conducted
by the Indian Air Force against a designated terrorist facility, PIB said the operation
underscored the IAF's precision strike capability, operational preparedness, and resolved to
deliver a calibrated response to terrorism.
This is Akash Wani giving you the news.

spreading lies and falsehoods about Jammu and Kashmir, asserting that the union territory
is and will always remain an integral and inalienable part of India. India exercised
its right of reply during a discussion on decolonization in the fourth committee of the
UN General Assembly in New York today.
Member of Parliament Mahima Kumar Maywar responded to a statement by Pakistan's representative
in a post on X in that the UN in New York said Maywar had accused Pakistan of misusing
the UN platform to spread false claims about Jammu and Kashmir.
It is regrettable that Pakistan continues to abuse this August forum by peddling
lies and falsehoods about the Indian Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir.
We call upon Pakistan to stop the grave and ongoing human right violation in the areas
illegally occupied by it, where the population is in open revolt against Pakistan's
needs, military occupation, repression, brutality, and illegal exploitation of resources.
Mahalaya is being observed today mocking the traditional invocation of Goddess Durga
and heralding the arrival of Durga Pujo, Bengal's biggest annual festival.
Here is a report from our Kolkata correspondent.
The day marks the culmination of Pithri Pakko, the fortnight dedicated to paying homage to
departed ancestors and the beginning of Devi Pakko, according to traditional Hindu
belief.
Devotees across the state are offering torpon on the banks of rivers and other water
bodies praying for the peace of their ancestors' souls.
Mahalaya is also synonymous with the timeless radio program Mohisha Shoromodini, broadcast
by Akashvani in the early hours of the day.
The program, featuring Sanskrit chants, devotional songs and narration by Birindra Krishna Bhadro,
has remained an integral part of Bengal's cultural heritage for generations.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi in a social media message said, we seek the blessings
of Mahadurga. May the blessings fill our society with happiness, compassion and hope. May there
be peace and prosperity all around. With the invocation of Goddess Durga, the countdown to Durga
puja begins, filling the air with devotion, anticipation and festive spirit. Shondipandash Gupta,
Abhisbanini, Kolkata.

The portals of Sri Hemkunt Sahib, the renowned Sikh pilgrimage site in Chamoli district of
Uttarakhand, were closed for winter today.
The final Arthasar prayer was performed at 12.30pm, following which the portals were closed
at 1 p.m. in accordance with religious traditions. The portals of Shri Hemgun Sahib were opened
to pilgrims on May 23, this year, during the pilgrimage season, around 280,000 devotees
paid obeisance at the sacred shrine.
